newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada energy production rises 3.2 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Canada energy production rises 3.2 pct in 1996.

text.p: Production of energy products in Canada rose 3.2 percent in 1996, the lowest rate of increase since 1993, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
The agency said the modest increase was primarily the result of slow export growth of 4.3 percent in 1996, the smallest increase since 1990.
Crude oil and natural gas exports to the United States increased in 1996 but at a slower rate than in previous years, the agency said.
Exports of crude oil rose 6.3 percent in 1996 compared with 8.0 percent a year earlier, mainly because of disruptions in sythentic crude oil production, StatsCan said.

Natural gas exports rose 1.3 percent in 1996, the lowest increase this decade. StatsCan pointed to limited pipeline capacity and reduced demand by U.S. electric utilities as the major reasons for weak natural gas exports.
A colder-than-normal winter in Canada prompted a 4.5 percent rise in energy consumption in 1996 compared with 1995, StatsCan said.
In the fourth quarter of 1996, energy production rose 2.9 percent over the same quarter a year earlier.
